system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

Verdane Care
Application: Full-Stack Engineer (TypeScript / React) – Patient Experience
Dear Verdane Care Hiring Team,
Your Patient Experience role closely matches my work building customer-facing onboarding
journeys with React, TypeScript, NestJS and PostgreSQL. At Älvgrind Fintech, I have
improved identity verification, accessibility and mobile performance across the frontend and
backend. That experience offers a practical foundation for Verdane Care’s appointment-booking
and intake features, where completing a task easily and reliably matters to the person using the
software.
I built a BankID verification flow covering QR codes, error states and retries; onboarding
conversion increased from 61% to 74%. We A/B tested the flow with 10% of traffic before
rolling it out fully. I also reduced mobile Largest Contentful Paint from 4.1 to 1.9 seconds and
implemented WCAG 2.1 AA audit fixes. These are directly relevant foundations for your focus
on low-end phones and WCAG 2.2 AA, without treating accessibility and performance as
separate from feature delivery.
My backend work includes migrating Express services to NestJS and building document uploads
with S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV scanning in Lambda, and status handling through SQS and
PostgreSQL. My current stack also includes Jest, Playwright, Docker and GitHub Actions,
alongside Storybook and Next.js for marketing pages. I collaborate with designers in Figma,
participate in production on-call support, and previously mentored coding bootcamp students.
This combination fits the breadth of a small squad delivering features end to end.
Verdane Care’s React-based design system and independently audited patient app provide a
concrete setting for this experience. I would welcome a conversation about how my work
improving onboarding journeys could contribute to simpler booking and intake experiences for
your patients.
Kind regards,
Oskar Haddad-Lindqvist

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
